text:
sam: heads up — saw a cluster-wide latency stutter at ~14:02 UTC today for model-a. p50 jumped ~180ms to ~450ms for ~90s.

evan: saw that. spike lines up with a scale-out (scale-controller) event. interestingly kernel selection churn in the logs during that window.

rachel: do we have KV cache hit-rate around that time? cold misses + kernel toggles would explain token path regressions.

mike: attaching short excerpt from node logs:
```
[14:02:11] scale-controller: requested 8 replicas -> provisioning
[14:02:12] kernel-manager: choose kernel opt_attn_v3 for model-a seq=512
[14:02:12] kernel-manager: fallback kernel compat_attn_v1 (quant mismatch)
[14:02:12] kv-cache: prefix miss for user:abc tokenkeys=0.42
[14:02:13] batching: heuristic changed from dynamic->aggressive batch_size=1->8
[14:02:13] latency: tail+50ms
```

sam: hmm batching heuristic flipped aggressively when new nodes joined. that caused single-request batches to be coalesced incorrectly.

evan: kernel toggling looks like a race: new nodes register different compiled kernels (opt_attn_v3) while old nodes serve compat_attn_v1; route chooser oscillates and requests get re-routed mid-stream — KV cache isn't shared during the handoff, so misses spike.

rachel: perf-bot flamegraph from the 14:02 window:
```
flamegraph top:
 - runtime_dispatch 35%
 - kernel_switch 22%
 - kv_lookup 18%
 - batch_assemble 12%
 - other 13%
```

mike: repro steps I used locally:
1) start 2 replica pool with compat kernel
2) trigger scale to 6 where build pipeline compiles opt kernel
3) send steady low-QPS requests that rely on KV prefix caching
result: p50 jumps and KV hit-rate drops ~3x during handoff.

sam: confirm this is different from prior warm-pool eviction cases — here it's a combination: (a) scale-controller starts nodes with different kernel binary versions, (b) batching heuristic has no hysteresis and flips immediately when node capacity changes, (c) KV cache instances are isolated so new node misses are expensive.

evan: quick mitigation options:
- pin kernel variant per-model across rollout (soft pin) so route chooser prefers existing kernel for X minutes
- add batching hysteresis: require sustained capacity change window before switching heuristic
- pre-warm KV cache during scale-up using async prefetch of common prefixes

rachel: I'll prototype a soft-pin in router: prefer same kernel until 30s after scale event. mike can we add a small delay before the batching heuristic flips (5s)?

mike: yes I can add a 5s hysteresis to the heuristic config and test in staging. also will add metrics to track kernel-switch rate.

deploy-bot: staging rollout started for heuristic-hysteresis v1 -> canary 10% (deploy id: dpl-8342)

perf-bot: alert suppressed for 30m while canary runs. historical baseline stashed.

sam: for KV prefetch I have a short script to sample top prefixes from recent traffic and bulk-populate new nodes' caches during provisioning. rachel, want that hooked into the scale flow?

rachel: yes. make it optional and gated by model config. prefer async prefetch with backoff.

evan: action items:
- rachel: router soft-pin prototype + test (owner)
- mike: batching hysteresis change + staging canary (owner)
- sam: KV prefetch script + integration proposal (owner)
- evan: add kernel-switch metric and dashboard, investigate compile pipeline to reduce variant drift

mike: will also record a short perf trace during the next canary and post it here.

sam: thanks all. keeping this thread open — if canary looks good we'll schedule a quick rollout to prod off-peak.

mike: quick note — batching hysteresis PR linked: https://git.internal/r/mike/heuristic-hysteresis/pull/7

rachel: router soft-pin draft: https://git.internal/r/rachel/router-soft-pin/ — tests pending.

evan: added a Grafana panel for kernel-switch rate and kv-hit-rate. dashboard: internal/gfx/runtime-kernel-ops

deploy-bot: staging canary completed: 10% -> 100% scheduled if no regressions in 15m.

sam: closing the loop — will post postmortem-ish summary if we see repeat. for now monitoring + mitigations in place. :thumbsup:
